instruction: Run a targeted perception pass on the original image, not the render. (1) Sample ink along the F→BC path, starting at F, to decide whether a dashed FG exists, and record its endpoints as measured ink, not as an extrapolated intersection. (2) Inspect the 12 px overhang past F and classify it as solid, dashed, or part of the continuation, and record where any style change occurs. (3) Crop label_06 to confirm the 'G' glyph and check for a vertex mark on BC near its position. Return the measured ink evidence and a yes/no result for each question. If perception confirms dashed ink from F to BC with a G label, the next stage is geometry: add point G at the measured BC foot, add a dashed segment FG with the measured style, bind label G to it, and split seg_AF at F so the overhang is resolved. If perception finds no dashed ink beyond F, route to review, because the critic's high-severity issue would then be wrong.
